comparisons.peer_topic: Aggregate government incentive commitments and specific international projects
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the company had aggregate government commitments of up to $3.4 billion through 2033, including $1.8 billion for a facility in India (funded 50% by central government, 20% by state) and up to $1.3 billion from Japan for DRAM production using EUV lithography.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose specific, multi-billion dollar unrecognized construction-related commitments under government agreements as of fiscal year 2024, though the nature of the obligation differs. Intel reports an unrecognized commitment to fund its share of Arizona SCIP construction costs with a remaining unfunded contribution of $10.5 billion. In contrast, Micron reports aggregate government commitments of up to $3.4 billion to be received through 2033 for facilities in India and Japan, which are contingent on performance conditions rather than representing a direct construction funding liability.

sentences.text: Other purchase commitments also include our unrecognized commitment to fund our respective share of the total construction costs of Arizona SCIP in connection with the definitive agreement entered into with Brookfield during 2022.
Our remaining unfunded contribution was $10.5 billion as of December 28, 2024.

In addition to the receivables and other noncurrent assets in the table above, as of August 29, 2024, we had aggregate commitments from various governmental entities of up to $3.4 billion to be received through 2033, subject to achievement of certain performance conditions.
The commitment amount includes $1.8 billion (150 billion Indian rupees) for the construction of a new assembly and test facility in Gujarat, India.
